summary: Draft Session Manager Kernel record. `ForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog` sits under `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager\\Kernel`, has an explicit repo-doc default of `0`, is absent on the observed clean baseline, produced an exact current-build string hit in `ntoskrnl.exe`, survived a write-and-reboot lightweight runtime batch as a candidate value of `1`, and now has dedicated live KVM local-KD proof that `KiForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog` exists on the running current build with value `0`. The lane is real, but still lacks an exact runtime registry read or a dedicated current-build caller/seeding proof.

validation_proof.exact_quote_or_path: Docs/system/system.md assigns `ForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog = 0` under `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager\\Kernel`, and later baseline, string, runtime, and live KD follow-ups keep the same value on the current-build research lane.
validation_proof.notes: This is enough to document the record as a real current-build candidate; the remaining blocker is exact reader/seeding proof rather than missing validation structure.

setting.name: Force Bugcheck For DPC Watchdog
setting.casual_explanation: This appears to be a kernel-level Session Manager setting related to DPC watchdog bugcheck behavior. It is not a normal end-user setting and is being tracked as a research candidate.
setting.why_people_change_it: Kernel researchers may inspect this value when investigating DPC watchdog policy, watchdog escalation behavior, or kernel timing diagnostics.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The value has a stronger than usual docs-first evidence chain, but it is still kernel-adjacent and not safe for general use. Current evidence is enough for a draft record, not for a published tweak.
setting.professional_notes: Repo docs assign `ForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog = 0` and tie the value to `KiForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog`. The docs-first kernel routing pass later kept it inside the `session-manager-kernel` exact-hit batch. The observed clean baseline then confirmed that `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager\\Kernel` exists while the value itself is absent. The broad current-build string batch found an exact Unicode hit for `ForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog` in `ntoskrnl.exe`. A later tools-hardened lightweight runtime lane wrote all 21 `Session Manager\\Kernel` batch values, including `ForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog = 1`, rebooted once, preserved shell health, and still returned `no-hit` for this specific candidate in the ETW-derived query surface. A dedicated KVM local-KD follow-up then resolved the live DPC watchdog symbol cluster and directly read `nt!KiForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog = 0` on the running current build, which aligns with the repo-doc default and is stronger than docs-plus-string evidence alone. The next proof step is no longer symbol existence; it is a current-build reader or seeding caller that explains whether the registry value is an active override or only a dormant/default-mapping lane.
